claim.pdf_says: Page 1018 (printed 988) opens with the script label and its ranges on consecutive lines: "Old_Italic:" / "10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F"
claim.markdown_says: The page-1018 block opens with a headless range, "10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F", with no "Old_Italic:" label. The label was pulled back onto the last line of the page-1017 block, where it is glued to the preceding script's ranges: "10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:" (ISO_COBOL.md line 40558).
claim.why_it_matters: Annex B (normative) "Characters permitted in user-defined words" is a label-to-code-point-range table. The union of code points is unchanged, but the binding of the range 10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F to the script Old_Italic is destroyed: read linearly the markdown shows Old_Hungarian's range line ending in a stray "Old_Italic:" token, followed by page furniture, followed by an unattributed range. Any mechanical extraction of the annex from the markdown mis-associates or drops the entry.

verdict.reasoning: Both quotations check out verbatim, but the deviation is page-break line-joining -- furniture/formatting, which the rubric excludes -- and it is not a page-1018 content defect. WHAT I VERIFIED DIRECTLY. (1) Rendered PDF p.1018 (printed 988) at 300 dpi: it does open with 'Old_Italic:' on its own line, then '10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F'. (2) Rendered PDF p.1017 (printed 987): it ends with 'Old_Hungarian:' / '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2' and 'Old_Italic:' is definitively NOT on it. (3) ISO_COBOL.md line 40558 is exactly '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:', and line 40564 -- the first content line of the page-1018 block -- is the headless '10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F'. So the label really did land on the far side of the page marker, and I initially read this as a genuine structural defect. A mechanical scan of the page boundaries then reversed that. WHY IT IS REFUTED. (a) NOTHING IS LOST OR ALTERED. I diffed all 16 script entries printed on PDF p.1018 (Old_Italic, Old_North_Arabian, Old_Permic, Old_Persian, Old_Sogdian, Old_South_Arabian, Old_Turkic, Oriya, Osage, Osmanya, Pahawh_Hmong, Palmyrene, Pau_Cin_Hau, Phags_Pa, Phoenician, Psalter_Pahlavi) against the markdown block: every label and every range matches character for character, including the two-line wrap of Oriya. (b) READING ORDER IS PRESERVED, SO THE BINDING IS NOT DESTROYED. The markdown token sequence is 'Old_Hungarian:' / '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2' / 'Old_Italic:' / [page anchor + running head] / '10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F'. That is the PDF's own sequence. 'Old_Italic:' still immediately follows Old_Hungarian's ranges and still immediately precedes its own; it did not jump over another entry. What changed is one line break becoming a space, and which side of the page marker the label sits on. The claim's 'the binding is destroyed' therefore overstates: read top to bottom, the markdown yields the correct association. (c) DECISIVE -- IT IS UNIFORM PIPELINE BEHAVIOR, NOT PAGE-1018 CONTENT. I scripted the test over every page anchor in the Annex B script-table region (19 anchors, md lines 40400-41400), checking each for a glued trailing '<Name>:' on the preceding line and a headless opening line after the anchor. The next page's first script label is hoisted back across the break at essentially every boundary in the table: glued at pages 1015 ('A984-A9B2 Kaithi:'), 1016 ('...10760-10767 Linear_B:'), 1017 ('10980-1099F Miao:'), 1018 ('...10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:'), 1019 ('10B80-10B91 Rejang:'), 1022 ('1A17-1A1B Buhid:'), 1023 ('0AFA-0AFF Gunjala_Gondi:'), 1024 ('...17E0-17E9 Khojki:'), 1025 ('...11650-11659 Mongolian:'), 1026 ('...A8D0-A8D9 Sharada:'); and hoisted-but-not-glued, sitting alone on its own line before the anchor, at 1020 ('Tai_Le:') and 1021 ('Yezidi:'). Exactly one boundary in the table transcribes cleanly, page 1027 ('Telugu:' correctly after the anchor). Every one of those boundaries also shows the corresponding headless opening line. Page 1018 is one instance of a 12-of-13 pattern, so filing it as a per-page content discrepancy would mint an identical ledger entry at nearly every page of the annex. (d) The claim's harm argument rests entirely on a hypothetical naive line-based extractor rather than on the two sources differing in content. Any consumer of Annex B must already strip the page anchors, the '## Page NNNN' headings, the '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' running heads and the '988 (c)ISO/IEC 2023' footers; once furniture is stripped and the stream rejoined, splitting on the '<Name>:' pattern recovers every binding correctly. That is a consumer-robustness requirement, not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. RESIDUAL, RECORDED HONESTLY: the joined line '10C80-10CB2, 10CC0-10CF2 Old_Italic:' does violate the table's otherwise-invariant 'label line, then range line' shape, and a strictly line-oriented reader would mis-bind it. That is worth one pipeline-level note about page-boundary line joining across the annex -- not a structural content finding against page 1018.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy; reject. The claim's two quotations are accurate, but nothing on page 1018 is missing, added, or reordered -- all 16 script entries match the PDF character for character, and 'Old_Italic:' is present on the adjacent line, still immediately preceded by Old_Hungarian's ranges and still immediately followed by its own range '10300-1031F, 1032D-1032F' in reading order. The sole difference is which side of the page-break furniture the label falls on, i.e. line joining at the page boundary, so the label-to-range binding survives in document order and the claim's 'the binding is destroyed' is an overstatement. It is also not specific to page 1018: a scan of all 19 page anchors in the Annex B script-table region shows the next page's first script label hoisted back across the break at 12 of the 13 in-table boundaries -- glued to the previous range line at pages 1015, 1016, 1017, 1018, 1019, 1022, 1023, 1024, 1025, 1026, and sitting alone above the anchor at 1020 and 1021 -- with only page 1027 ('Telugu:') transcribing cleanly. If tracked at all, track it once as a pipeline-level page-boundary line-joining note for Annex B, with the guidance that any extractor must strip the page anchors and running heads (which it must do regardless) and split on the '<Name>:' pattern rather than pairing strictly by line.
